newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil BNDES to kick off Eletrobras sale.
newsitem.headline: Brazil BNDES to kick off Eletrobras sale.

text.p: Brazil's National Development Bank (BNDES) will kick off Tuesday Eletrobras' privatization process when consultants begin bidding for mandates to advise on the sale of Furnas and Eletrosul, a BNDES spokesman said.
Furnas and Eletrosul, two of the four power generating units controlled by holding company Eletrobras, are expected to be privatized late this year or early 1998.
The Brazil's National Development Bank will receive the proposals from consultants at 1430 local time/1730 GMT and it will announce the pre-qualified advisors on April 11, the spokesman said.
The spokesman could not say when the bank hopes to announce the winning bidders, but local newspapers speculate the winners will be announced by the end of next month.

The consulting firms will be competing to advise the bank on two services. The first service, or "A" service contract, consists of a financial evaluation of the two companies, while the "B" service includes financial evaluation and designing a privatization model for the firms, he said.

Furnas operates in Brazil's major southeastern states of Sao Paulo, Rio de Janeiro and Minas Gerais and accounts for 15 percent the country's power generating capacity and 29 percent of Eletrobras's capacity. It has a power capacity of 8,123 megawatts.
Eletrosul has a power generating capacity of 3,222 megawatts and operates in the southern states of Parana, Santa Catarina, Rio Grande do Sul and center-south state of Mato Grosso do Sul.
